title.zh: 卷六十八 列傳第五十八 趙知禮 蔡景歷 宗元饒 韓子高 華皎 劉師知 謝岐 毛喜 沈君理 陸山才
title.en: Volume 68 Biographies 58: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai
title.raw: 卷六十八 列傳第五十八 趙知禮 蔡景歷 宗元饒 韓子高 華皎 劉師知 謝岐 毛喜 沈君理 陸山才 Volume 68 Biographies 58: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十八

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Biography 58

sentences.zh: 趙知禮蔡景曆宗元饒韓子高華皎劉師知謝岐毛喜沈君理陸山才

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, and Lu Shancai

sentences.zh: 趙知禮字齊旦，天水隴西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili, styled Qidan, was a man of Longxi in Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, whose courtesy name was Qidan, came from Longxi in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父孝穆，梁候官令。

translations.literal: His father Xiaomu was Magistrate of Houguan under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaomu had served as magistrate of Houguan under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 知禮涉獵文史，善書翰。

translations.literal: Zhili ranged through literary and historical texts and was skilled in calligraphy and letters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili read widely in literature and history and was accomplished at writing and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝之討元景仲也，或薦之，引為書記。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen campaigned against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him, and he was brought in as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wu-di was campaigning against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended Zhili, and he was taken on as a secretary.

sentences.zh: 知禮為文贍速，每占授軍書，下筆便就，率皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Zhili's writing was rich and swift; whenever he was assigned military documents, his brush finished at once, and they invariably met approval.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili wrote with fluency and speed; whenever he was told to draft military dispatches, he would finish at a stroke, and his work invariably pleased his superiors.

sentences.zh: 由是恒侍左右，深被委任，當時計畫，莫不預焉。

translations.literal: From this he constantly attended at the left hand, was deeply entrusted, and in the plans of the time there was none in which he did not take part.
translations.idiomatic: He was henceforth always at the emperor's side, deeply trusted, and involved in every major plan of the day.

sentences.zh: 武帝征侯景，至白茅灣，上表于梁元帝及與王僧辯論軍事，其文並知禮所制。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Hou Jing and reached Baimao Bay, the memorial to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the discussion of military affairs with Wang Senbian were both composed by Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Hou Jing and reached Baimao Bay, the memorial to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the exchanges on military affairs with Wang Senbian were both written by Zhili.

sentences.zh: 及景平，授中書侍郎，封始平縣子。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 陳受命，位散騎常侍、太府卿，權知領軍事。

translations.literal: When Chen received the Mandate, he held the posts of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Grand Steward, and acted as supervisor of army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen dynasty was founded, he served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Grand Steward, with provisional charge of military administration.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiāncái, his noble rank was advanced to Baron.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiāncái (560), he was promoted to baron.

sentences.zh: 王琳平，授吳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, he was appointed Governor of Wú Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin was defeated, he was appointed governor of Wu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知禮沈靜有謀謨，每軍國大事，文帝輒令璽書問之。

translations.literal: Zhili was calm and possessed of stratagems; whenever there were great affairs of state and army, Emperor Wén would send sealed letters to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili was reserved and thoughtful; on every major military or political matter, Emperor Wen would consult him by sealed edict.

sentences.zh: 再遷右將軍，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to General of the Right and concurrently General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to General of the Right and concurrently commanded the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Attendant-in-Ordinary, with the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and given the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子元恭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuangong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuangong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 蔡景曆字茂世，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Cai Jingli, styled Maoshi, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jingli, courtesy name Maoshi, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖點，梁尚書左戶侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dian was Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Left Household under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dian had been Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Left Household under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父大同，輕車岳陽王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Datong was Recorder of the Prince of Yueyang, Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: His father Datong had served as recorder on the staff of the Prince of Yueyang, Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 景曆少俊爽，有孝行，家貧好學，善尺牘，工草隸。

translations.literal: Jingli in youth was handsome and open, had filial conduct, was poor but loved learning, was skilled in letters, and excelled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jingli was bright and spirited, known for filial piety; though his family was poor he loved learning, wrote excellent letters, and was accomplished in cursive and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 為海陽令，政有能名。

translations.literal: He served as Magistrate of Haiyang; his administration had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Haiyang he earned a reputation for capable government.

sentences.zh: 在侯景中，與南康嗣王會理通，謀匡復，事泄被執，賊党王偉保護之，獲免，因客遊京口。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing he associated with the Heir of Nankang, Huili, and plotted restoration; the affair leaked and he was seized; the rebel partisan Wang Wei protected him and he was spared, and he then traveled as a guest to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he was in contact with Huili, heir of Nankang, and plotted to restore the dynasty; when the plot was exposed he was arrested, but the rebel Wang Wei protected him and he escaped execution, afterward living as a guest in Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，陳武帝鎮朱方，素聞其名，以書要之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Wu of Chen was stationed at Zhufang and had long heard his name; he summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Chen Wu-di, then stationed at Zhufang, had long heard of him and invited him by letter.

sentences.zh: 景曆對使人答書，筆不停綴，文無所改。

translations.literal: Jingli replied to the envoy's letter; his brush did not pause, and the text needed no revision.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli composed his reply to the envoy without pausing his brush, and not a word needed changing.

sentences.zh: 帝得書，甚加欽賞，即日授征北府中記室參軍，仍領記室。

translations.literal: The Emperor received the letter and greatly admired it; that same day he appointed him Army Recorder in the Northern Campaign Headquarters, and he continued to head the recorder's office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed and that same day appointed him army recorder in the northern campaign headquarters, with continuing charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王昌為吳興太守，帝以鄉里父老，尊卑有數，恐昌年少接對乖禮，乃遣景曆輔之。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang, Chang, was Governor of Wuxing; the Emperor, because among the elders of the homeland senior and junior had their order, feared that Chang in his youth would receive and reply improperly, and therefore sent Jingli to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xian of Hengyang, Chang, became governor of Wuxing, the emperor feared that the young prince would mishandle protocol among the local gentry and sent Jingli to advise him.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，還掌記室。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era he returned to head the recorder's office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chengsheng reign he again headed the recorder's office.

sentences.zh: 武帝將討王僧辯，獨與侯安都等數人謀之，景曆弗之知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was about to attack Wang Senbian, he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu prepared to move against Wang Senbian, he confided only in Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli was not told.

sentences.zh: 部分既畢，召令草檄，景曆援筆立成，辭義感激，事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: When the dispositions were complete, he was summoned to draft the proclamation; Jingli took up the brush and finished at once; the language was stirring, and everything met approval.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dispositions were set, he was called on to draft the proclamation; Jingli wrote it at a stroke in stirring language that fully satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，遷秘書監、中書通事舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Jingli was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Attending Clerk for Comprehensive Affairs of the Secretariat, in charge of edicts and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication he was made Director of the Secretariat and Attending Clerk for Comprehensive Affairs, with charge of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，坐妻弟受周寶安餉馬，為御史中丞沈炯所劾，降為中書侍郎，舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding, because his wife's younger brother had received horses as a gift from Zhou Bao'an, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong and demoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat, while retaining his clerkship.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding (558), his wife's younger brother was found to have accepted horses from Zhou Bao'an; impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong, Jingli was demoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat but kept his clerk's duties.

sentences.zh: 三年，武帝崩。

translations.literal: In the third year, Emperor Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 時外有強寇，文帝鎮南皖，朝無重臣，宣後呼景曆及江大權、杜棱定議，秘不發喪，疾召文帝。

translations.literal: At the time there were powerful enemies outside; Emperor Wen was stationed at Southern Wan; the court had no weighty ministers; Empress Xuan summoned Jingli, Jiang Daquan, and Du Leng to decide policy, kept the death secret, and urgently summoned Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful enemies threatened from without, Emperor Wen was posted at Southern Wan, and no senior minister remained at court; Empress Xuan called in Jingli, Jiang Daquan, and Du Leng, concealed the death, and urgently summoned Wen.

sentences.zh: 景曆躬共宦者及內人密營斂服，時既暑熱，須營梓宮，恐斤斧之聲聞外，乃以蠟為秘器，文詔依舊宣行。

translations.literal: Jingli personally joined eunuchs and inner attendants in secretly preparing the burial garments; as it was already hot summer and a catalpa coffin had to be made, fearing that the sound of axes would be heard outside, they used wax for the inner coffin, and written edicts continued to be issued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli worked with eunuchs and palace women to prepare the burial privately; because summer heat required a wooden coffin whose hammering might be heard outside, they used a wax inner coffin while edicts continued to issue as usual.

sentences.zh: 華皎反，以景曆為武勝將軍、吳明徹軍司。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was made General Who Establishes Martial Victory and army aide to Wu Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Victory and staff officer to Wu Mingche.

sentences.zh: 皎平，明徹於軍中輒戮安成內史楊文通，又受降人馬仗有不分明，景曆又坐不能匡正被收。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Mingche on his own authority executed Yang Wentong, Administrator of Ancheng, in the army camp, and also received horses and arms from surrendered men in unclear circumstances; Jingli again was charged for failing to correct this and was taken into custody.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao's defeat, Mingche summarily executed Yang Wentong, administrator of Ancheng, in camp and took horses and arms from surrendering troops in questionable fashion; Jingli was arrested for failing to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 久之獲宥。

translations.literal: After a long while he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，累遷通直散騎常侍、中書通事舍人，掌詔誥，仍復封邑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jingli was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Unimpeded Service, and Attending Clerk for Comprehensive Affairs, in charge of edicts, and his fief was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he rose to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Unimpeded Service, and Attending Clerk, again directing edicts, and his fief was restored.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，都督吳明徹北侵，所向克捷，大破周梁士彥于呂梁，方進圍彭城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, Supervisor Wu Mingche invaded north; wherever he went he prevailed, and at Lüliang he greatly defeated Liang Shiyan of Zhou; he was just advancing to besiege Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573), Wu Mingche marched north as supreme commander, winning every engagement and crushing Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Lüliang before moving to besiege Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝銳意河南，以為指麾可定，景曆稱師老將驕，不宜過窮遠略。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought that a wave of the hand could settle them; Jingli said the army was weary and the generals arrogant, and that one should not press a distant campaign too far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was bent on recovering the south bank of the Yellow River and believed victory was at hand; Jingli warned that the army was tired and the generals overconfident, and that the campaign should not be pushed too far.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其沮眾，大怒，猶以朝廷舊臣，不加深罪，出為豫章內史。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated his damping of morale and was greatly angered, but because he was an old minister of the court did not deepen the punishment and sent him out as Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered at this discouragement of the troops, refrained from harsher punishment only because Jingli was a longtime minister and instead sent him out as administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 未行，為飛章所劾，以在省之日，贓汙狼籍，帝令有司案問，景曆但承其半。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was impeached by flying memorial; it was charged that during his days at the Secretariat corruption was widespread; the Emperor ordered the authorities to investigate, and Jingli admitted only half.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, an urgent memorial accused him of widespread corruption during his time at court; ordered to answer the charges, Jingli admitted only half.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞宗元饒奏免景曆所居官，徙居會稽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao memorialized to remove Jingli from his posts and banish him to live in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao then memorialized for his dismissal and exile to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹敗，帝追憶景曆前言，即日追還，以為征南鄱陽王諮議。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche was defeated, the Emperor recalled Jingli's earlier words and that same day summoned him back, appointing him Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Southern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche was defeated, the emperor remembered Jingli's warning and recalled him the same day as adviser to the Prince of Poyang on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 數日，遷員外散騎常侍，兼御史中丞，復本爵封，入守度支尚書。

translations.literal: Within days he was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, his original rank and fief were restored, and he entered to serve as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was made Extraordinary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with his rank and fief restored, and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 舊式拜官在午後，景曆拜日，適逢輿駕幸玄武觀，在位皆侍宴，帝恐景曆不預，特令早拜，其見重如此。

translations.literal: By old custom investiture took place in the afternoon; on the day of Jingli's investiture the imperial carriage happened to visit the Xuanwu Observatory, and all officials in attendance were serving at the banquet; the Emperor feared Jingli would not participate and specially ordered an early investiture—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture normally took place in the afternoon, but on Jingli's appointment day the emperor was feasting at the Xuanwu Observatory with the whole court; fearing Jingli would miss the ceremony, he ordered an early investiture—such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈太常卿，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously he was given Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous title Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies with the posthumous name Reverent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改葬，重贈中領軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when he was reburied, he was again given General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, at his reburial, he was posthumously made General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was given joint sacrifice in the temple court of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming (587) he was granted a place in sacrifices at Emperor Wu's temple.

sentences.zh: 二年，車駕親幸其宅，重贈景曆侍中、中撫將軍，諡曰忠敬，給鼓吹一部，於墓所立碑。

translations.literal: In the second year the imperial carriage personally visited his residence; Jingli was again given Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Pacification Army, with the posthumous title Loyal and Reverent, granted one set of martial music, and a stele was erected at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor visited his home in person and posthumously made him Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Pacification Army, with the posthumous name Loyal and Reverent, granted martial music, and ordered a stele at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 景曆屬文，不尚雕靡，而長於敘事，應機敏速，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Jingli in composition did not esteem ornate excess but excelled in narrative; he responded to occasions with swift intelligence and was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His prose avoided ornament and excelled in narrative; quick and apt in every situation, he was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 子征嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 江大權字伯謀，濟陽考城人，位少府，封四會縣伯。

translations.literal: Jiang Daquan, styled Bomou, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang; he held the post of Minister of the Palace Storehouses and was enfeoffed as Baron of Sihui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Daquan, courtesy name Bomou, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang; he served as Minister of the Palace Storehouses and was enfeoffed as Baron of Sihui.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，卒於通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian he died while holding Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Unimpeded Service.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taijian (570) while serving as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Unimpeded Service.

sentences.zh: 征字希祥，幼聰敏，精識強記。

translations.literal: Zheng, styled Xixiang, in youth was clever and keen, with penetrating knowledge and strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, courtesy name Xixiang, was clever as a child, with a sharp mind and remarkable memory.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，詣梁吏部尚書河南褚翔，嗟其穎悟。

translations.literal: At age six he visited Chu Xiang of Henan, Minister of Personnel under the Liang, who sighed at his brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: At six he visited Chu Xiang of Henan, Liang Minister of Personnel, who marveled at his precocity.

sentences.zh: 七歲丁母憂，居喪如成人禮。

translations.literal: At seven he entered mourning for his mother and observed the mourning rites like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, when his mother died, he observed mourning with the gravity of an adult.

sentences.zh: 繼母劉氏，性悍忌，視之不以道，征供侍益謹，初無怨色。

translations.literal: His stepmother, Lady Liu, was by nature fierce and jealous and did not treat him properly; Zheng in serving her became all the more careful and at first showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother Lady Liu was harsh and jealous and treated him badly, yet Zheng served her only more carefully and never showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 征本名覽，景曆以其有王祥之性，更名字焉。

translations.literal: Zheng's original name was Lan; Jingli, because he had the nature of Wang Xiang, changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Lan; Jingli, seeing in him the filial spirit of Wang Xiang, gave him the name Zheng.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝為南徐州，召補迎主簿，尋授太學博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen was at Southern Xuzhou, he was summoned to fill the post of Registrar for Reception and soon appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wu-di was governor of Southern Xuzhou, Zheng was summoned as registrar for reception and soon made Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 太建中，累遷太子中舍人，兼東宮領直，襲封新豐侯。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Head of Eastern Palace Duty, and inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: During Taijian he rose to Attendant of the Heir Apparent and head of eastern palace duty, inheriting the marquisate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 至德中，位太子中庶子、中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era he held the posts of Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Attending Clerk of the Secretariat, in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhide he served as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Attending Clerk of the Secretariat, directing imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋授左戶尚書，與僕射江總知撰五禮事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Left Household and, with Vice Director Jiang Zong, directed the compilation of the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of the Left Household and, with Vice Director Jiang Zong, oversaw compilation of the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 後主器其才幹，任寄日重。

translations.literal: The Later Lord valued his talent and ability, and his trust and commission grew daily heavier.
translations.idiomatic: The later emperor valued his ability and relied on him ever more heavily.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，每十日一往東宮，于皇太子前論述古今得喪及當時政務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel; every ten days he would go once to the Eastern Palace and before the Crown Prince discourse on the gains and losses of past and present and on current government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Minister of Personnel, he visited the eastern palace every ten days to lecture the crown prince on history and current affairs.

sentences.zh: 又敕以廷尉寺獄，事無大小，取征議決。

translations.literal: He was also ordered that in the prisons of the Court of Judicial Review, matters great and small should take Zheng's deliberation for decision.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered that all cases in the Court of Judicial Review, large or small, be decided on his advice.

sentences.zh: 俄敕遣徵收募兵士，自為部曲，征善撫恤，得物情，旬月之間，眾近一萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to send Zheng to recruit soldiers; he formed his own command; Zheng was skilled in comforting and caring, won the hearts of men, and within a month or so his force approached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to raise troops under his own command; Zheng treated them well, won their loyalty, and within a month had nearly ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 位望既重，兼聲位熏灼，物議咸忌憚之。

translations.literal: His position and prestige were already weighty, and together with his fame and rank he blazed; public opinion all feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His rank and influence were now immense, his fame dazzling, and opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 尋徙中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中書清簡無事，或云征有怨言，後主聞之大怒，收奪人馬，將誅之，左右致諫，獲免。

translations.literal: The Secretariat was pure and simple with little business; someone said Zheng had words of complaint; the Later Lord heard and was greatly angered, seized his men and horses, and was about to execute him; attendants remonstrated and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat had little to do; rumor said Zheng grumbled at his idleness; the later emperor flew into a rage, stripped him of men and horses, and would have executed him but for the remonstrance of his attendants.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，隋軍濟江，後主以征有幹用，令權知中領軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming the Sui army crossed the river; the Later Lord, because Zheng had practical ability, ordered him provisionally to supervise the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming (589), when Sui forces crossed the Yangzi, the later emperor, trusting Zheng's ability, put him in provisional charge of the central army.

sentences.zh: 征日夜勤苦，備盡心力，後主嘉焉，謂曰：「事寧有以相報」。

translations.literal: Zheng toiled day and night with bitter diligence and exhausted his mind and strength; the Later Lord praised him and said, "When affairs are settled there will be reward."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng labored day and night with all his strength; the emperor praised him, saying, "When this is over I will repay you."

sentences.zh: 及決戰于鍾山南岡，敕征守宮城西北大營，尋令督眾軍戰事。

translations.literal: When the decisive battle was fought on the southern ridge of Zhong Mountain, he was ordered to guard the great camp northwest of the palace city, and soon was ordered to supervise the military affairs of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the decisive battle on the southern slope of Zhong Mountain he was ordered to hold the great camp northwest of the palace, then to direct all field operations.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隨例入長安。

translations.literal: When Chen perished, he followed the usual practice and entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he was taken to Chang'an like the other captives.

sentences.zh: 征美容儀，有口辯，多所詳究。

translations.literal: Zheng had a handsome appearance, was skilled in debate, and had investigated many matters in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was handsome, eloquent, and widely learned.

sentences.zh: 至於士流官宦，陳宗戚屬，及當朝制度，憲章儀軌，戶口風俗，山川土地，問無不對。

translations.literal: As for the gentry and official class, Chen imperial clansmen and relatives, and the institutions of the current court, statutes and ritual norms, household registers and customs, mountains and rivers and lands—there was no question to which he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: On the gentry, Chen imperial kin, court institutions, ritual codes, population registers, local customs, and geography, he could answer any question.

sentences.zh: 然性頗便佞進取，不能以退素自業。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was rather given to flattery and advancement and could not make his calling in modest withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was ambitious and ingratiating and could not content himself with a modest life.

sentences.zh: 初拜吏部尚書，啟後主借鼓吹，後主謂所司曰：「鼓吹軍樂，有功乃授，蔡征不自量揆，紊我朝章。

translations.literal: When he was first appointed Minister of Personnel, he memorialized the Later Lord to borrow martial music; the Later Lord told the responsible office, "Martial music is military music; it is granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not measure himself and disorders our court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On first becoming Minister of Personnel he asked the emperor for martial music; the emperor told his officers, "Martial music is a military honor granted only for merit. Cai Zheng overreaches and disrupts our regulations.

sentences.zh: 然其父景曆既有締構之功，宜且如啟，拜訖即追還。

translations.literal: Yet his father Jingli already had merit in founding and structuring; for the moment let it be as he requests, but after the investiture immediately recall it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet his father Jingli helped found the dynasty; grant it for now, but recall the music as soon as the appointment ceremony ends."

sentences.zh: 」征不修廉隅，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Zheng did not cultivate the corners of integrity—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng lacked integrity in matters like these.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聞其敏贍，召見顧問，言輒會旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his quickness and richness and summoned him for consultation; his words invariably met the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui, hearing of his brilliance, summoned him for counsel; his answers always pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 然累年不調，久之，除太常丞。

translations.literal: Yet for many years he received no appointment; after a long while he was made Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for years he received no substantive post; at last he was made Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 曆尚書戶部儀曹郎，轉給事郎，卒。

translations.literal: He passed through Attendant of the Household Department, Rites Section, of the Ministry of Revenue, was transferred to Attendant for Submission of Memorials, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant of the Household Department, Rites Section, then as Attendant for Submission of Memorials, and died.

sentences.zh: 子翼，位司徒屬。

translations.literal: His son Yi held the post of Attendant of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi served as attendant of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 入隋，為東宮學士。

translations.literal: When they entered Sui, he became a Scholar of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he became a scholar of the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 宗元饒，南郡江陵人也。

translations.literal: Zong Yuanrao was a man of Jiangling in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yuanrao was from Jiangling in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，以孝聞。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning as a youth and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為征南府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He served the Liang as External Army Recorder of the Southern Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as external army recorder on the southern campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 及司徒王僧辯幕府初建，元饒與沛國劉師知同為主簿。

translations.literal: When the secretariat of Minister of Education Wang Senbian was first established, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei were both chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Senbian first formed his staff, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei both served as chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，稍遷廷尉卿、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the abdication, he was gradually promoted to Minister of Justice and Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chen founding he rose to Minister of Justice and Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 宣帝初，軍國務廣，事無巨細，一以咨之，台省號為稱職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuan's reign military and state affairs were broad; matters great and small were all referred to him, and the ministries were said to be fulfilling their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuan's reign, with military and civil affairs pressing, every matter large or small was referred to him, and the bureaucracy was said to be functioning well.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，知五禮事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and directed the affairs of the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Censor-in-Chief with charge of the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 時合州刺史陳褒贓汙狼籍，遣使就渚斂魚，又令人於六郡乞米，百姓甚苦之，元饒劾奏免之。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Bao, Governor of He Prefecture, had corruption spread everywhere; he sent envoys to the shallows to collect fish and also had men beg rice in six commanderies; the common people suffered greatly; Yuanrao impeached and memorialized for his removal.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Bao of He prefecture was notoriously corrupt, extorting fish at the shore and sending men to beg grain across six commanderies; Yuanrao impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守武陵王伯禮、豫章內史南康嗣王方泰等，驕蹇放橫，元饒案奏，皆見削黜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wuling, Boli, Governor of Wuxing, and the Heir of Nankang, Fangtai, Administrator of Yuzhang, and others were arrogant, obstinate, and overbearing; Yuanrao investigated and memorialized, and all were demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Boli of Wuling, governor of Wuxing, and Fangtai, heir of Nankang and administrator of Yuzhang, among others, were arrogant and abusive; Yuanrao prosecuted them all and they were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 元饒性公平，善持法，諳曉故事，明練政體，吏有犯法，政不便時，及於名教不足者，隨事糾正，多所裨益。

translations.literal: Yuanrao by nature was fair and just, skilled in upholding the law, versed in precedents, and clear in the substance of government; when officials violated the law, when policy was inconvenient to the times, or when ritual teaching was insufficient, he corrected matters as they arose and brought much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Fair and firm in law, versed in precedent and clear on administration, he corrected illegal officials, impractical policies, and breaches of ritual wherever he found them, to great public benefit.

sentences.zh: 遷南康內史，以秩米三千餘斛助人租課，存問高年，拯救乏絕，百姓甚賴焉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Nankang; with more than three thousand hu of his salary grain he aided people's rent and tax payments, inquired after the aged, and rescued those in want; the common people greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: As administrator of Nankang he gave more than three thousand hu of his salary grain to help people pay taxes, comforted the elderly, and relieved the destitute; the people depended on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 以課最入朝，詔加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Because his administration ranked highest he entered the court; an edict added Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court for outstanding administration, he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry by edict.

sentences.zh: 後為吏部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: Later he became Minister of Personnel and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Minister of Personnel and died in office.

sentences.zh: 韓子高，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Han Zigao was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zigao was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 家本微賤。

translations.literal: His family was originally of humble status.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of humble origin.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，寓都下。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he lodged in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he lived in the capital.

sentences.zh: 景平，陳文帝出守吳興，子高年十六，為總角，容貌美麗，狀似婦人，於淮渚附部伍寄載欲還鄉里，文帝見而問曰：「能事我乎？

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen of Chen went out to guard Wuxing; Zigao was sixteen, in the age of the topknot, with beautiful features like a woman's; at the Huai ford he attached himself to a unit for passage wishing to return home; the Emperor saw him and asked, "Can you serve me?"
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Chen Wen-di went to govern Wuxing; Zigao was sixteen, still wearing the youth's topknot, strikingly beautiful and almost feminine in appearance. At a Huai River crossing he joined a convoy bound for home, and when the emperor saw him he asked, "Will you serve me?"

sentences.zh: 」子高許諾。

translations.literal: " Zigao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao agreed.

sentences.zh: 子高本名蠻子，帝改名之。

translations.literal: Zigao's original name was Manzi; the Emperor changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Manzi; the emperor gave him the name Zigao.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，恒執備身刀及傳酒炙。

translations.literal: By nature he was respectful and careful, always holding the bodyguard saber and serving wine and roasted meat.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and attentive, he always carried the emperor's sidearm and served wine and food.

sentences.zh: 帝性急，子高恒會意旨。

translations.literal: The Emperor was impatient by nature; Zigao always grasped his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was quick-tempered, but Zigao always anticipated his wishes.

sentences.zh: 稍長，習騎射，頗有膽決，願為將帥。

translations.literal: As he grew somewhat older he practiced riding and archery, had considerable daring and resolution, and wished to become a general.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he learned riding and archery, showed real courage, and aspired to command troops.

sentences.zh: 及平杜龕，配以士卒。

translations.literal: When Du Kan was pacified, soldiers were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Du Kan was defeated, he was given a command of troops.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚愛之，未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen loved him greatly and he never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen favored him deeply and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗夢騎馬登山，路危欲墮，子高推捧而升。

translations.literal: The Emperor once dreamed of riding a horse up a mountain; the path was perilous and he was about to fall, but Zigao pushed and supported him until he ascended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once dreamed he was riding uphill on a dangerous path about to fall, and Zigao lifted him safely to the summit.

sentences.zh: 文帝之討張彪也，沈泰等先降，帝據有州城，周文育鎮北郭香岩寺，張彪自剡縣夜還襲城，文帝自北門出，倉卒闇夕，軍人擾亂，唯子高在側。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen attacked Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others surrendered first; the Emperor held the prefectural city; Zhou Wenyü garrisoned Xiangyan Temple in the northern suburb; Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city; the Emperor went out the north gate in haste at dark dusk; the soldiers were in turmoil; only Zigao was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others surrendered first and Wen held the city while Zhou Wenyü garrisoned Xiangyan Temple in the northern suburb. Zhang Biao struck by night from Shan county; the emperor fled through the north gate in the dark confusion with only Zigao beside him.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃遣子高自亂兵中往見文育，反命酬答，於闇中又往慰勞眾軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent Zigao through the disorderly troops to see Wenyü, return with reply, and in the darkness go again to comfort and encourage the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zigao through the chaos to Zhou Wenyü and back with his answer, then out again in the dark to rally the troops.

sentences.zh: 文帝散兵稍集，子高引入文育營，因共立柵。

translations.literal: The Emperor's scattered troops gradually gathered; Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they erected palisades.
translations.idiomatic: As scattered forces reassembled, Zigao brought the emperor into Wenyü's camp and they threw up defenses together.

sentences.zh: 明日敗彪，彪奔松山，浙東平。

translations.literal: The next day they defeated Biao; Biao fled to Song Mountain, and eastern Zhe was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they defeated Biao, who fled to Song Mountain, and eastern Zhe was pacified.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃分麾下多配子高，子高亦輕財禮士，歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: The Emperor then assigned many of his subordinates to Zigao; Zigao also treated wealth lightly and honored scholars, and those who came to him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Zigao many of his own followers; generous and respectful of talent, Zigao attracted a large following.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，除右軍將軍，封文招縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Zigao was made General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen succeeded to the throne, Zigao was made General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 及王琳平，子高所統益多，將士依附之，其有所論進，帝皆任使焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, those under Zigao's command grew ever more numerous; officers and soldiers attached themselves to him, and whatever he recommended the Emperor employed.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin was defeated, Zigao's command grew; officers and men flocked to him, and the emperor adopted every man he recommended.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiāncái he became General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tiāncái he was made General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝不豫，入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was unwell, he entered to attend with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen fell ill, he attended him at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was given Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor acceded, Zigao was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宣帝入輔，子高兵權過重，深不自安，好參訪台閣，又求出為衡、廣諸鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Zigao's military authority was too weighty and he was deeply ill at ease; he liked to visit the ministries and also sought to go out as commander of Heng, Guang, and other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan became regent, Zigao's military power made him uneasy; he frequented the ministries and sought a post in Hengzhou, Guangzhou, or another frontier command.

sentences.zh: 光大元年八月，前上虞縣令陸昉及子高軍主告其謀反，宣帝在尚書省，因召文武在位議立皇太子，子高預焉，執送廷尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Guangda, the former Magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and Zigao's army commander reported that he plotted rebellion; Emperor Xuan was at the Masters of Writing and therefore summoned civil and military officials present to discuss establishing the crown prince; Zigao was among them, seized and sent to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Guangda, former magistrate Lu Fang and one of Zigao's commanders accused him of treason. Emperor Xuan, at the Masters of Writing, summoned the court to discuss the crown prince; Zigao attended, was arrested, and sent to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 其夕與到仲舉同賜死。

translations.literal: That same evening he was granted death together with Dao Zhongju.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was executed along with Dao Zhongju.

sentences.zh: 父延慶及子弟並原宥。

translations.literal: His father Yanqing and his sons and younger brothers were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanqing and his brothers and sons were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 王琳東下，皎隨侯瑱拒之。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin marched east, Jiao followed Hou Jin to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin marched east, Jiao followed Hou Jin in resisting him.

sentences.zh: 琳平，知江州事。

translations.literal: When Lin was pacified, he directed the affairs of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's defeat he administered Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 後隨都督吳明徹征周迪，迪平，以功進爵為侯，仍授都督、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed Supervisor Wu Mingche in campaigning against Zhou Di; when Di was pacified, for merit his rank was advanced to Marquis, and he was appointed Supervisor and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Wu Mingche's campaign against Zhou Di; after Di's defeat he was promoted to marquis and made supervisor and governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 皎起自下吏，善營產業，又征川洞，多致銅鼓及生口，並送都下。

translations.literal: Jiao rose from a low clerk; he was skilled at building estates, and also campaigned in river valleys and caves, bringing in many bronze drums and captives, all sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from a minor clerk, Jiao was skilled at amassing wealth; campaigning in the hill country he sent many bronze drums and captives to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，改封重安縣公。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Chong'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor acceded, Jiao was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chong'an.

sentences.zh: 韓子高誅後，皎內不自安，光大元年，密啟求廣州，以觀時主意。

translations.literal: After Han Zigao was executed, Jiao was inwardly ill at ease; in the first year of Guangda he secretly memorialized requesting Guangzhou to observe the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Zigao's execution Jiao grew anxious; in the first year of Guangda he secretly asked for Guangzhou to test the court's intentions.

sentences.zh: 宣帝偽許之，而詔書未出。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan falsely agreed, but the edict had not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan pretended to agree, but no edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 皎亦遣使引周兵，又崇奉梁明帝，士馬甚盛。

translations.literal: Jiao also sent envoys to bring in Zhou troops and furthermore honored Liang Ming-di; his soldiers and horses were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao also invited Zhou forces and proclaimed allegiance to Liang Ming-di; his army grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 詔乃以吳明徹為湘州刺史，實欲以輕兵襲之。

translations.literal: An edict then made Wu Mingche Governor of Xiang Province, in reality intending to strike him with light troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Wu Mingche governor of Xiang province, intending a surprise attack with light forces.

sentences.zh: 慮皎先發，乃前遣明徹率眾三萬，乘金翅直趣郢州，又遣撫軍大將軍淳于量率眾五萬，乘大艦繼之。

translations.literal: Fearing Jiao would strike first, they first sent Mingche leading thirty thousand men, riding the Golden Wings straight for Yingzhou, and also sent Pacification Army Grand General Chunyu Liang leading fifty thousand men in great ships to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jiao would move first, they sent Mingche ahead with thirty thousand men in swift vessels straight for Yingzhou, and Pacification Army Grand General Chunyu Liang with fifty thousand in large ships behind.

sentences.zh: 時梁明帝遣水軍為皎聲援，周武帝遣衛公宇文直頓魯山，又遣柱國長湖西元定攻圍郢州。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Ming-di sent a navy as vocal support for Jiao; Emperor Wu of Zhou sent Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi stationed at Lushan, and also sent Pillar of State Yuan Ding of Western Changhu to attack and besiege Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ming-di sent a fleet to support Jiao; Zhou Wu-di posted Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi at Lushan and sent Pillar of State Yuan Ding of Western Changhu to besiege Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁明帝授皎司空，巴州刺史戴僧朔、衡陽內史任蠻奴、巴陵內史潘智虔、岳陽太守章昭裕、桂陽太守曹宣、湘東太守錢明，並隸於皎。

translations.literal: Liang Ming-di gave Jiao Minister of Works; Dai Sengshuo, Governor of Ba; Ren Mannu, Administrator of Hengyang; Pan Zhiqian, Administrator of Baling; Zhang Zhaoyu, Administrator of Yueyang; Cao Xuan, Administrator of Guiyang; and Qian Ming, Administrator of Xiangdong—all were subordinate to Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ming-di made Jiao Minister of Works; the governors and administrators Dai Sengshuo of Ba, Ren Mannu of Hengyang, Pan Zhiqian of Baling, Zhang Zhaoyu of Yueyang, Cao Xuan of Guiyang, and Qian Ming of Xiangdong all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 又長沙太守曹慶等本隸皎下，因為之用。

translations.literal: Moreover Cao Qing, Administrator of Changsha, and others had originally been under Jiao and therefore served him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qing of Changsha and others who had already been under Jiao joined him as well.

sentences.zh: 帝恐上流宰守並為皎扇惑，乃下詔曲赦湘、巴二州，其賊主帥節將，並許開恩出首。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared that upstream governors and guards would all be incited and deluded by Jiao; he therefore issued an edict of special pardon for the two provinces of Xiang and Ba; rebel chiefs, commanders, and garrison generals were all permitted to show mercy and come forward.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing upstream officials would rally to Jiao, the emperor offered a special pardon in Xiang and Ba provinces, inviting rebel leaders and garrison commanders to surrender.

sentences.zh: 皎以大艦載薪，因風放火，俄而風轉自焚，皎大敗，乃與戴僧朔奔江陵。

translations.literal: Jiao loaded fuel on great ships and, using the wind, set fire; soon the wind turned and they burned themselves; Jiao was greatly defeated and then fled with Dai Sengshuo to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao loaded his great ships with fuel and tried to burn the Chen fleet, but the wind shifted and his own ships caught fire; utterly defeated, he fled with Dai Sengshuo to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元定等無復船渡，步趣巴陵，巴陵城已為陳軍所據，乃降，送於建鄴。

translations.literal: Yuan Ding and others had no more ships to cross; they marched toward Baling; Baling city was already held by Chen troops, and they surrendered and were sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding and his men, unable to cross by ship, marched on Baling, found it already in Chen hands, surrendered, and were sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 皎遂終於江陵，其黨並誅，唯任蠻奴、章昭裕、曹宣、劉廣業獲免。

translations.literal: Jiao then died at Jiangling; his partisans were all executed; only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao died at Jiangling; his followers were executed, though Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.

sentences.zh: 劉師知，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shizhi was a man of Xiang in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi was from Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 家本素族。

translations.literal: His family was originally of plain lineage.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of modest lineage.

sentences.zh: 祖奚之，齊淮南太守，以善政聞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xizhi was Governor of Huainan under Qi and was known for good government.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xizhi, governor of Huainan under Qi, was known for good administration.

sentences.zh: 父景彥，梁司農卿。

translations.literal: His father Jingyan was Minister of Agriculture under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingyan served as Minister of Agriculture under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 師知本名師智，以與敬帝諱同，改焉。

translations.literal: Shizhi's original name was Shizhi; because it was the same as the taboo name of Emperor Jing, it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Shizhi, changed to avoid the taboo of Emperor Jing of Liang.

sentences.zh: 好學，有當務才，博涉書傳，工文筆，善儀體，台閣故事，多所詳悉。

translations.literal: He loved learning, had talent for pressing affairs, ranged broadly through books and records, was skilled in literary composition, was adept at ritual forms, and was well versed in many precedents of the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted scholar with practical talent, he read widely, wrote well, mastered court ritual, and knew institutional precedent in detail.

sentences.zh: 紹泰初，陳武帝入輔，以師知為中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai, when Emperor Wu of Chen entered as regent, Shizhi was made Attending Clerk of the Secretariat, in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaotai, when Chen Wu-di became regent, Shizhi was made Attending Clerk of the Secretariat with charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 時兵亂後，朝儀多闕，武帝為丞相及加九錫並受禪，其儀注多師知所定。

translations.literal: At the time, after military chaos, court ritual was largely lacking; when the Emperor was Chancellor, received the Nine Bestowals, and accepted the abdication, the ritual protocols were largely set by Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars much court ritual had been lost; Shizhi drew up most of the protocols for Wu-di's chancellorship, the Nine Bestowals, and the abdication.

sentences.zh: 梁敬帝在內殿，師知常侍左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Liang was in the inner hall; Shizhi constantly attended at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Emperor Jing was confined in the inner palace, Shizhi was constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 及將加害，師知詐帝令出，帝覺，遶床走曰：「師知賣我，陳霸先反。

translations.literal: When they were about to kill him, Shizhi deceived the Emperor with an order to go out; the Emperor perceived it, ran around the bed, and said, "Shizhi has sold me; Chen Baxian rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment came to kill him, Shizhi tricked the emperor into leaving the chamber. The emperor realized what was happening and cried as he ran around the bed, "Shizhi has betrayed me! Chen Baxian is in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 我本不須作天子，何意見殺。

translations.literal: I originally had no need to be Son of Heaven—why do you mean to kill me?"
translations.idiomatic: I never wanted to be emperor—why must you kill me?"

sentences.zh: 」師知執帝衣，行事者加刃焉。

translations.literal: Shizhi seized the Emperor's robe, and those carrying out the deed applied the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi held the emperor fast while the assassins struck.

sentences.zh: 既而報陳武帝曰：「事已了。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he reported to Emperor Wu of Chen, "The affair is finished."
translations.idiomatic: He then reported to Chen Wu-di, "It is done."

sentences.zh: 」武帝曰：「卿乃忠於我，後莫復爾。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "You have been loyal to me; hereafter do not do so again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have served me faithfully—but never do such a thing again."

sentences.zh: 」師知不對。

translations.literal: Shizhi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi made no answer.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，仍兼舍人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, he still concurrently served as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu-di took the throne, Shizhi retained his clerkship.

sentences.zh: 性疏簡，與物多忤，雖位宦不遷，而任遇甚重，其所獻替，皆有弘益。

translations.literal: By nature he was plain and simple and often at odds with others; although his rank and office did not advance, his trust and commission were very weighty, and what he offered and withdrew all had broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and often at odds with others, he advanced little in rank yet was deeply trusted, and his counsel consistently benefited the state.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，六日成服，時朝臣共議大行皇帝靈座俠御人衣服吉凶之制，博士沈文阿議宜服吉，師知議云：「既稱成服，本備喪禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died, on the sixth day mourning garments were completed; at the time the court ministers together discussed the regulations for auspicious and inauspicious dress of those attending the late emperor's spirit seat; Erudite Shen Wena argued that auspicious dress should be worn; Shizhi argued, "Since it is called completing mourning garments, it fundamentally prepares funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, the court completed the six-day mourning observance and debated whether attendants at the late emperor's spirit seat should wear auspicious or mourning dress. Erudite Shen Wena argued for auspicious dress; Shizhi replied, "Once mourning garments are completed, full funeral rites apply.

sentences.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，成服，俠侍之官，悉著衰斬，唯著鎧不異，此即可擬。

translations.literal: According to the case when Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, when mourning garments were completed, the officials in attendance all wore the hemmed sackcloth of the highest mourning, only those wearing armor unchanged—this may be taken as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, attendants at the completion of mourning all wore full sackcloth except those in armor—this precedent should govern.

sentences.zh: 愚謂六日成服，俠靈座須服衰絰。

translations.literal: I hold that on the sixth day when mourning garments are completed, those attending the spirit seat must wear sackcloth with hempen bands.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that on the sixth day, attendants at the spirit seat must wear full mourning with hemp bands."

sentences.zh: 」中書舍人蔡景曆、江德藻、謝岐等同師知議。

translations.literal: Attending Clerks Cai Jingli, Jiang Dezao, and Xie Qi agreed with Shizhi's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Clerks Cai Jingli, Jiang Dezao, and Xie Qi sided with Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 時以二議不同，乃啟取左丞徐陵決斷。

translations.literal: Because the two opinions differed, they memorialized to have Left Assistant Xu Ling decide.
translations.idiomatic: The two views deadlocked, and the matter was referred to Left Assistant Xu Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵云：「案山陵鹵簿吉部伍中，公卿以下導引者，爰及武賁、鼓吹、執蓋、奉車，並是吉服，豈容俠禦獨為衰絰？

translations.literal: Ling said, "According to the auspicious section of the mountain-tomb procession, from dukes and ministers down, those who lead the way, as well as the martial guards, martial music, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants—all wear auspicious dress; how can attendants alone wear sackcloth with hempen bands?
translations.idiomatic: Ling replied, "In the auspicious section of the tomb procession, from ministers down through guards, musicians, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants, all wear auspicious dress. How can attendants alone wear mourning?

sentences.zh: 若言公卿胥吏並服衰絰，此與梓宮部伍有何差別？

translations.literal: If one says that dukes, ministers, clerks, and functionaries all wear sackcloth with hempen bands, what difference is there from the cortège of the inner coffin?
translations.idiomatic: If ministers and clerks all wore mourning, how would they differ from the cortège of the inner coffin?

sentences.zh: 若言文物並吉，司事者凶，豈容衽絰而奉華蓋，衰衣而升玉路邪？

translations.literal: If one says the ritual regalia are all auspicious but those who perform the rites are inauspicious, how can one wear the hemmed band while bearing the flowered canopy, or ascend the jade chariot road in mourning garments?
translations.idiomatic: If regalia were auspicious but performers in mourning, could one bear the imperial canopy in sackcloth or mount the jade chariot in mourning robes?"

sentences.zh: 同博士議。

translations.literal: He agreed with the Erudite's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He sided with the erudite.

sentences.zh: 」謝岐議曰：「靈筵祔宗廟，梓宮祔山陵，實如左丞議。

translations.literal: Xie Qi argued, "The spirit seat is enshrined in the ancestral temple and the inner coffin in the mountain tomb—this is indeed as the Left Assistant said.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi argued, "The spirit seat goes to the ancestral temple and the inner coffin to the tomb, as the Left Assistant said.

sentences.zh: 但山陵鹵簿，備有吉凶，從靈輿者儀服無變，從梓宮者皆服苴衰，爰至士禮，悉同此制。

translations.literal: But the mountain-tomb procession has both auspicious and inauspicious parts; those following the spirit carriage do not change ritual dress, while those following the inner coffin all wear coarse sackcloth—even down to the rites for scholars, all follow this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: But the tomb procession has both auspicious and mourning sections: followers of the spirit carriage keep auspicious dress, while followers of the inner coffin wear coarse sackcloth, even in the rites for common scholars.

sentences.zh: 此自是山陵之儀，非關成服。

translations.literal: This is inherently the rite of the mountain tomb and is not related to completing mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: That is tomb ritual, not the completion of mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 今謂梓宮靈扆，共在西階，稱為成服，亦無鹵簿，直是爰自胥吏，上至王公，四海之內，必備衰絰。

translations.literal: Now it is said that the inner coffin and spirit screen are together on the western steps, called completing mourning garments, and there is no procession either—simply from clerks and functionaries up to princes and dukes, within the four seas, all must prepare sackcloth with hempen bands.
translations.idiomatic: Here the inner coffin and spirit screen stand together on the western steps with no procession—only the completion of mourning garments—yet from clerks to princes throughout the realm all must wear full mourning.

sentences.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，略是成例，豈容凡百士庶，悉皆服重，而侍中至於武衛，最是近官，反鳴玉紆青，與平吉不異？

translations.literal: According to the case when Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, this is roughly the established example; how can common scholars and commoners all wear heavy mourning, while from Attendant-in-Ordinary down to the Martial Guard—the closest officials—instead jade sounds and blue sashes, no different from ordinary auspicious times?
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, that was the precedent. Can every scholar and commoner wear heavy mourning while the closest officials, from Attendants-in-Ordinary to the Martial Guard, wear jade and blue sashes as on any ordinary day?"

sentences.zh: 左丞既推以山陵事，愚意或謂與成服有殊。

translations.literal: Since the Left Assistant has pushed this as a matter of the mountain tomb, my humble opinion perhaps holds that it differs from completing mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant treats this as tomb ritual, but I believe completing mourning garments is a different matter."

sentences.zh: 」陵重答云：「老病屬纊，不能多說。

translations.literal: Ling replied again, "Old and ill, I lie with the death shroud and cannot say much.
translations.idiomatic: Ling replied again, "Old and ill, I lie near death and cannot debate at length.

sentences.zh: 古人爭議，多成怨府，傅玄見尤于晉代，王商取陷於漢朝。

translations.literal: When men of old disputed, they often became houses of resentment; Fu Xuan was blamed in the Jin, Wang Shang was trapped in the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient disputants often made lasting enemies—Fu Xuan suffered in Jin, Wang Shang in Han.

sentences.zh: 謹自三緘，敬同高命。

translations.literal: I respectfully seal my mouth thrice and reverently accept your lofty command.
translations.idiomatic: I seal my lips thrice and bow to your judgment.

sentences.zh: 若萬一不死，猶得展言，庶與群賢，更申揚榷。

translations.literal: If by the slightest chance I do not die, I may still unfold my words and perhaps with the assembled worthies renew the exposition and weighing.
translations.idiomatic: If by chance I survive, I may yet argue the point again with the assembled worthies."

sentences.zh: 」文阿猶執所見，眾議不能決，乃具錄二議奏聞，上從師知議。

translations.literal: Wena still held to his view; the assembly could not decide, and they therefore fully recorded both opinions and memorialized; the sovereign followed Shizhi's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Wena held to his view; unable to decide, the court recorded both opinions and memorialized the emperor, who ruled with Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚卿，舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies, his clerkship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of Ceremonies while retaining his clerkship.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiāncái he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiāncái he was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 尋起為中書舍人，復掌詔誥。

translations.literal: Soon he was reappointed Attending Clerk of the Secretariat and again directed edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Attending Clerk and again directed edicts.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，文帝不豫，師知與尚書僕射到仲舉等入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiānkāng, when Emperor Wen was unwell, Shizhi and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Dao Zhongju and others entered to attend with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiānkāng, when Emperor Wen fell ill, Shizhi and Vice Director Dao Zhongju attended him at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，豫顧命。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, he was included in the final testament.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Shizhi was named in the final testament.

sentences.zh: 宣帝入輔，師知與仲舉等遣舍人殷不佞矯詔令宣帝還東府，事覺，於北獄賜死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Shizhi and Zhongju and others sent Attending Clerk Yin Buniu with a forged edict ordering Emperor Xuan back to the Eastern Palace; when the affair was discovered, he was granted death in the northern prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan became regent, Shizhi and Zhongju forged an edict through Clerk Yin Buniu ordering him back to the eastern palace; exposed, Shizhi was executed in the northern prison.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝敕師知撰起居注，自永定二年秋至天嘉元年為十卷。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Wen ordered Shizhi to compile the Diary of Activity and Repose, from autumn of the second year of Yongding to the first year of Tiāncái, in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had ordered Shizhi to compile the court diary from autumn of the second year of Yongding through the first year of Tiāncái, ten juan in all.

sentences.zh: 謝岐，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Xie Qi was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父達，梁太學博士。

translations.literal: His father Da was Erudite of the Imperial University under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da was Erudite of the Imperial University under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 弟嶠，篤學，為通儒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qiao was devoted to learning and became a comprehensive scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qiao was a devoted scholar and recognized authority on the classics.

sentences.zh: 毛喜字伯武，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xi, styled Bowu, was a man of Yangwu in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xi, courtesy name Bowu, was from Yangwu in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖稱，梁散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Attendant-in-Ordinary of Scattered Cavalry under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng was Attendant-in-Ordinary of Scattered Cavalry under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父棲忠，中權司馬。

translations.literal: His father Qizhong was Marshal of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qizhong was Marshal of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗謂宣帝曰：「我諸子皆以'伯'為名，汝諸子宜用'叔'為稱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once said to Emperor Xuan, "All my sons take 'Bo' in their names; your sons should use 'Shu' in their style.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told Emperor Xuan, "My sons all use Bo in their names; your sons should use Shu."

sentences.zh: 」宣帝以訪喜，喜即條自古名賢杜叔英、虞叔卿等二十餘人以啟之，文帝稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan consulted Xi; Xi at once listed more than twenty famous men of antiquity such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and presented them; Emperor Wen praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan asked Xi, who listed more than twenty historical figures such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing; Emperor Wen approved.

sentences.zh: 文帝崩，廢帝沖昧，宣帝錄尚書輔政，僕射到仲舉等矯太后令，遣宣帝還東府，當時疑懼，無敢厝言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor was young and ignorant; Emperor Xuan recorded affairs as regent; Vice Director Dao Zhongju and others forged an order of the Empress Dowager sending Emperor Xuan back to the Eastern Palace; at the time all were fearful and doubtful, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, the young deposed emperor reigned and Emperor Xuan served as regent. Vice Director Dao Zhongju forged an empress dowager's order sending Xuan back to the eastern palace; the court was terrified and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 喜即馳入，謂宣帝曰：「今日之言，必非太后之意，宗社至重，願加三思。

translations.literal: Xi at once rode in and said to Emperor Xuan, "Today's words cannot be the Empress Dowager's intent; the altars of state are supremely weighty—I beg you to reflect thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Xi rode in at once and told Emperor Xuan, "This order cannot truly come from the empress dowager. The fate of the dynasty hangs on your decision—think carefully."

sentences.zh: 」竟如其策。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he had strategized.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍韓子高始與仲舉通謀，其事未發，喜謂宣帝曰：「宜簡人馬配與子高，並賜鐵炭，使修器甲。

translations.literal: General of the Right Guard Han Zigao had at first plotted with Zhongju; the affair had not yet broken; Xi said to Emperor Xuan, "You should select men and horses to assign to Zigao and also grant him iron and charcoal to have him repair weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Guard Han Zigao was plotting with Zhongju before the plot was exposed. Xi told Emperor Xuan, "You should assign men and horses to Zigao and supply iron and charcoal for armor—"

sentences.zh: 」宣帝曰：「子高即欲收執，何更如是？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan said, "I am about to seize Zigao—why do this further?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan said, "I mean to arrest Zigao—why arm him further?"

sentences.zh: 」喜曰：「山陵始畢，邊寇尚多，而子高受委前朝，名為杖順，宜推心安誘，使不自疑，圖之一壯士之力耳。

translations.literal: Xi said, "The mountain tomb has only just been completed and border enemies are still many; Zigao was entrusted by the former court and is known as upholding obedience—you should reassure and entice him so he does not suspect himself; to take him is but the strength of one brave man."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The imperial tomb is barely finished and enemies still threaten the borders. Zigao served the previous reign and claims loyalty—reassure him so he does not grow suspicious; then one bold man can bring him down."

sentences.zh: 」宣帝卒行其計。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan in the end carried out his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 及得淮南之地，喜陳安邊之術，宣帝納之，即日施行。

translations.literal: When they obtained the lands south of the Huai, Xi presented methods for securing the borders; Emperor Xuan accepted them and implemented them that same day.
translations.idiomatic: After recovering the Huai region, Xi proposed border-security measures that Emperor Xuan adopted the same day.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲進兵彭、汴，以問喜，喜以為「淮左新平，邊人未輯，周氏始吞齊國，難與爭鋒，未若安人保境，斯久長之術也」。

translations.literal: The Emperor also wished to advance troops to Peng and Bian and consulted Xi; Xi held that "the left bank of the Huai is newly pacified and the border people are not yet settled; the house of Zhou has just swallowed Qi and is hard to contend with in the spearhead—better to settle the people and guard the borders; this is the method of long endurance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also planned to march on Pengcheng and Bian and asked Xi, who replied, "The Huai region is newly pacified and the frontier people are unsettled; Zhou has just absorbed Qi and is too strong to challenge. Secure the people and hold the borders—that is the path to lasting peace."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹卒俘于周。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche in the end was captured by Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche was eventually captured by Zhou.

sentences.zh: 喜後曆丹陽尹，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Xi later served as Prefect of Danyang and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Xi later served as prefect of Danyang and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝崩，叔陵構逆，敕中庶子陸瓊宣旨，令南北諸軍皆取喜處分。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Shuling plotted rebellion; an order was given for Junior Mentor Lu Qiong to proclaim the intent that all armies north and south should take Xi's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died and Shuling rebelled, Junior Mentor Lu Qiong was ordered to proclaim that all northern and southern armies should follow Xi's command.

sentences.zh: 賊平，加侍中。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was given Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 初，宣帝委政於喜，喜數有諫爭，事並見從。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted government to Xi; Xi repeatedly remonstrated and argued, and his matters were all followed.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted him with government; Xi remonstrated repeatedly and was usually heeded.

sentences.zh: 自明徹敗後，帝深悔不用其言，謂袁憲曰：「一不用喜計，遂令至此。

translations.literal: After Mingche's defeat the Emperor deeply regretted not using his words and said to Yuan Xian, "Had I not used Xi's plan once, it would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: After Mingche's defeat the emperor deeply regretted ignoring him and told Yuan Xian, "Had I listened to Xi, we would not be here."

sentences.zh: 」由是益見親重，喜乃言無回避。

translations.literal: From this he was all the more seen as close and weighty, and Xi then spoke without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was trusted all the more, and Xi spoke without holding back.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子好酒德，每共親幸人為長夜之宴，喜嘗言之宣帝，太子遂銜之，即位後稍見疏遠。

translations.literal: At the time the Crown Prince loved wine and virtue and often with favored intimates held all-night banquets; Xi once spoke of this to Emperor Xuan, and the Crown Prince therefore bore a grudge; after accession he was gradually seen at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince loved wine and often held all-night revels with his favorites; Xi reported this to Emperor Xuan, and the prince bore a grudge; after accession he gradually distanced Xi.

sentences.zh: 及被始興王傷，創愈，置酒引江總以下，展樂賦詩，醉酣而命喜。

translations.literal: When he was wounded by the Prince of Shixing and his wound healed, he set out wine and summoned Jiang Zong and those below, displayed music and composed poems, and when drunk and flushed ordered Xi.
translations.idiomatic: After being wounded by the Prince of Shixing and recovering, he held a feast for Jiang Zong and others with music and poetry, and when drunk summoned Xi.

sentences.zh: 于時山陵初畢，未及踰年，喜見之不懌，欲諫而後主已醉。

translations.literal: At that time the mountain tomb had only just been completed and a year had not yet passed; Xi saw this and was displeased, wished to remonstrate, but the Later Lord was already drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb had only just been completed and less than a year had passed; Xi was displeased and wished to remonstrate, but the later emperor was already drunk.

sentences.zh: 喜言心疾，僕於階下，移出省中。

translations.literal: Xi claimed heart illness, collapsed on the steps, and was moved out of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xi claimed a heart ailment, collapsed on the steps, and was carried from the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 後主醒，乃謂江總曰：「我悔召毛喜，知其無病，但欲阻我歡宴，非我所為耳。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord awoke, he said to Jiang Zong, "I regret summoning Mao Xi; I know he has no illness—he only wanted to obstruct my merry feast; this is not what I would do."
translations.idiomatic: When the later emperor sobered, he told Jiang Zong, "I regret calling Mao Xi. He is not ill—he only wanted to spoil my feast. That is not how I treat my guests."

sentences.zh: 」乃與司馬申謀曰：「此人負氣，吾欲將乞鄱陽兄弟，聽其報讎，可乎？

translations.literal: He then plotted with Marshal Shen, saying, "This man is proud in spirit; I wish to give him to the brothers of Poyang and let him take revenge—would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Marshal Shen, "This man is proud. I want to hand him to the princes of Poyang to take revenge—would that do?"

sentences.zh: 「對曰：「終不為官用，願如聖旨。

translations.literal: Shen replied, "He will never serve in office again; I wish it as Your Majesty commands."
translations.idiomatic: Shen replied, "He will never serve the court again. Your Majesty's will be done."

sentences.zh: 」傅縡爭之曰：「若許報讎，欲置先皇何地？

translations.literal: Fu Zai argued, "If revenge is permitted, where is the late emperor to be placed?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zai objected, "If you allow revenge, what becomes of the late emperor's honor?"

sentences.zh: 」後主曰：「當與一小郡，勿令見人事耳。」

translations.literal: The Later Lord said, "He shall be given a small commandery and not allowed to see human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The later emperor said, "Give him a small prefecture and keep him from court affairs."

sentences.zh: 至德元年，授永嘉內史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 喜至郡，不受奉秩，政弘清靜，人吏安之。

translations.literal: When Xi reached the commandery he did not accept salary and stipend; his government was broad, pure, and quiet, and the people and officials were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he refused his salary, governed with quiet integrity, and officials and people alike were content.

sentences.zh: 遇豐州刺史章大寶舉兵反，郡與豐州接，而素無備，喜乃修城隍器械，又遣兵援建安。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dabao, Governor of Feng Province, raised troops in rebellion, the commandery bordered Feng Province and had long been unprepared; Xi therefore repaired walls and moats and weapons, and also sent troops to aid Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Zhang Dabao of Feng province rebelled, Yongjia bordered Feng and was unprepared; Xi fortified the walls, repaired arms, and sent troops to aid Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授南安內史。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Administrator of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated he was made administrator of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，徵為光祿大夫，領左驍騎將軍，道卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry of the Left; he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming he was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and General of Valiant Cavalry of the Left but died en route.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子處沖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chuchong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuchong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 沈君理字仲倫，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Shen Junli, styled Zhonglun, was a man of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Junli, courtesy name Zhonglun, was from Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖僧畟，梁左戶尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengji was Minister of the Left Household under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengji was Minister of the Left Household under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父巡，元帝時位少府卿。

translations.literal: His father Xun, in the time of Emperor Yuan, held the post of Minister of the Palace Storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun served as Minister of the Palace Storehouses under Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 魏平荊州，梁宣帝署金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jing Province, Liang Emperor Xuan appointed him Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei conquered Jing province, Liang Emperor Xuan appointed him Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 君理美風儀，博涉有識鑒。

translations.literal: Junli had fine bearing and manner, ranged broadly, and had discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Junli was handsome and dignified, widely learned, and discerning.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝鎮南徐州，巡遣君理致謁，深見器重，命尚會稽長公主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen was stationed at Southern Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli to pay respects; he was deeply valued and esteemed and was ordered to marry the Eldest Princess of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wu-di was posted at Southern Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli to pay his respects; deeply impressed, the emperor gave him the eldest princess of Kuaiji in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，拜駙馬都尉，封永安亭侯，為吳郡太守。
