translations.literal: When the Emperor received the abdication, Junli was made Commandant of the Horse for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an ting, and made Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding he was made Commandant of the Horse for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an, and appointed governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 時兵革未甯，百姓荒弊，君理總集士卒，修飾器械，深以幹理見稱。

translations.literal: At the time arms and armor were not yet at peace and the common people were desolate and impoverished; Junli gathered soldiers, repaired and adorned weapons, and was deeply praised for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: With war still unsettled and the people destitute, he gathered troops, repaired arms, and won renown for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，累遷左戶尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen he rose to Minister of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，為東陽太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiāncái he became Governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tiāncái he became governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，以父憂去職，自請往荊州迎柩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiānkāng he left office for his father's mourning and himself requested to go to Jing Province to meet the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiānkāng he left office to mourn his father and asked to go to Jing province to fetch the coffin.

sentences.zh: 朝議以在位重臣，難令出境，乃遣長兄君嚴往焉。

translations.literal: The court discussed that as a weighty minister in office it was hard to order him beyond the borders, and therefore sent his elder brother Junyan in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that a senior minister could not leave the realm, and sent his elder brother Junyan instead.

sentences.zh: 及還，將葬，詔贈巡侍中、領軍將軍，諡曰敬子。

translations.literal: When they returned and were about to bury him, an edict posthumously gave Xun Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Leads the Army, with the posthumous title Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, before the burial, Xun was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Leads the Army with the posthumous name Reverent.

sentences.zh: 太建中，歷位太子詹事，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he passed through the posts of Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During Taijian he served as Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以君理女為皇太子妃，賜爵望蔡縣侯，位侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan made Junli's daughter the Crown Princess and granted him the rank of Marquis of Wangcai county; he held the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan made his daughter crown princess, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wangcai, and appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈翊左將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰貞憲。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given General of the Left Who Assists and Grand Prefect with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Upright and Lawful.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of the Left Who Assists and Grand Prefect with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Upright and Lawful.

sentences.zh: 君理弟君高、君公。

translations.literal: Junli's younger brothers were Jungau and Jungong.
translations.idiomatic: Junli's younger brothers were Jungau and Jungong.

sentences.zh: 君高字季高，少知名，性剛直，有吏能。

translations.literal: Jungau, styled Jigao, was known from youth, was by nature upright and firm, and had ability as an administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jungau, courtesy name Jigao, was known from youth for his upright character and administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 位衛尉卿，平越中郎將、都督、廣州刺史，甚得人和。

translations.literal: He held the post of Minister of the Guards, Middle General Who Pacifies the South, Supervisor, and Governor of Guang Province, and greatly won the harmony of men.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Guards, Middle General Who Pacifies the South, supervisor, and governor of Guang province, and won wide loyalty.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡祁子。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Reverent.

sentences.zh: 君公自梁元帝敗後，常在江陵。

translations.literal: Jungong from the time Emperor Yuan of Liang was defeated constantly remained at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan of Liang's defeat, Jungong remained at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 禎明中，與蕭瓛、蕭岩叛隋歸陳，後主擢為太子詹事。

translations.literal: In Zhenming he, with Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan, rebelled against Sui and returned to Chen; the Later Lord promoted him to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming he defected from Sui to Chen with Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan, and the later emperor made him Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 君公博學有才辯，善談論，後主深器之。

translations.literal: Jungong was broadly learned, had talent and eloquence, was skilled in discourse, and the Later Lord deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and eloquent, skilled in debate, he was deeply valued by the later emperor.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，文帝以其叛亡，命斬于建康。

translations.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui; Emperor Wen, because of his defection and flight, ordered him beheaded at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui service, but Emperor Wen ordered him executed at Jiankang for his defection.

sentences.zh: 君理第五叔邁，亦方正有幹局，位通直散騎常侍，侍東宮。

translations.literal: Junli's fifth uncle Mai was also upright and had administrative capacity; he held the post of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Unimpeded Service, and attended the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Junli's fifth uncle Mai was likewise upright and capable; he served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Unimpeded Service, attending the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 陸山才字孔章，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shancai, styled Kongzhang, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shancai, courtesy name Kongzhang, was from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖翁寶，梁尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wengbao was Attendant of the Water Section under the Masters of Writing of the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wengbao was Attendant of the Water Section under the Liang Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父泛，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Fan was Grand Master of Leisurely Dissemination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan was Grand Master of Leisurely Dissemination.

sentences.zh: 山才倜儻，好尚文史，范陽張纘、纘弟綰並欽重之。

translations.literal: Shancai was free and bold, loved and esteemed literature and history, and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and Zuan's younger brother Wan both admired and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and free-spirited, he loved literature and history; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and his brother Wan both held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，都督周文育出鎮南豫州，不知書疏，以山才為長史，政事悉以委之。

translations.literal: In Shaotai, Supervisor Zhou Wenyü went out to garrison Southern Yuzhou and did not understand documents and letters; he made Shancai Chief of Staff and entrusted all government affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai, when Zhou Wenyü was posted to Southern Yuzhou and could not manage documents himself, he made Shancai chief of staff and entrusted all affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 文育南討，克蕭勃，禽歐陽頠，計畫多出山才。

translations.literal: Wenyü campaigned south, overcame Xiao Bo, and captured Ouyang Yi; the plans mostly came from Shancai.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenyü's southern campaign against Xiao Bo and Ouyang Yi, most of the strategy came from Shancai.

sentences.zh: 後文育重鎮豫章金口，山才復為鎮南長史、豫章太守。

translations.literal: Later Wenyü again garrisoned Jinkou in Yuzhang; Shancai again became Chief of Staff for the Southern Garrison and Governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyü again garrisoned Jinkou in Yuzhang, Shancai again served as southern staff chief and governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，曇朗囚山才等，送于王琳。

translations.literal: Wenyü was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Tanlang imprisoned Shancai and others and sent them to Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü was killed by Xiong Tanlang, who imprisoned Shancai and sent him to Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 未至，而侯安都敗琳將常眾愛，由是山才獲反。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai, and thereby Shancai was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached Lin, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai, and Shancai was able to return.

sentences.zh: 累遷度支尚書，坐侍宴與蔡景曆言語過差，為有司所奏，免官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Revenue; he sat in attendance at a banquet and in speech with Cai Jingli exceeded proper bounds, was impeached by the responsible authorities, and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Revenue but was dismissed after speaking improperly to Cai Jingli at a court banquet.

sentences.zh: 尋授散騎常侍，遷西陽、武昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and transferred to be Governor of the two commanderies of Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and governor of Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Simple.

sentences.zh: 論曰：趙知禮、蔡景曆屬陳武經綸之日，居文房書記之任，此乃宋、齊之初傅亮、王儉之職。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli belonged to the days when Chen Wu laid out the realm; they held the duties of secretarial recorders in the literary chamber—this was the office of Fu Liang and Wang Jian at the beginning of Song and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli served during Chen Wu-di's founding, in the secretarial posts once held by Fu Liang and Wang Jian under Song and Qi.

sentences.zh: 若乃校其才用，理不同年，而卒能膺務濟時，蓋其遇也。

translations.literal: If one compares their talent and employment, by principle they were not of the same generation, yet in the end they were able to undertake affairs and aid the times—this was perhaps their opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Their talents were not of the same order, yet both served the times well—such was their fortune.

sentences.zh: 希祥勞臣之子，才名自致，跡涉便佞，貞介所羞。

translations.literal: Xixiang was the son of a meritorious minister; fame and talent he achieved himself, but his tracks touched flattery and advancement—what the upright despise.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiang, son of a meritorious minister, won fame by his own gifts, yet his career smacked of flattery—shameful to the upright.

sentences.zh: 元饒始終任遇，無虧公道，名位自卒，其殆優乎。

translations.literal: Yuanrao from beginning to end received appointment and trust without loss to public justice; fame and rank ended with him—perhaps he was superior.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrao served throughout without compromising justice and died in honor—perhaps the finest of them.

sentences.zh: 子高權重為戮，亦其宜也。

translations.literal: Zigao, his authority weighty, was executed—this too was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao's execution for excessive power was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 華皎經綸雲始，既蹈元功，殷憂之辰，自同勁草，雖致奔敗，未足為非。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao from the beginning of laying out the realm trod the original merit; in days of deep sorrow he was himself like tough grass; although he met defeat and flight, it is not enough to call it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao shared in the founding and stood firm in hard times; though he ended in defeat, he was not without honor.

sentences.zh: 師知送往多闕，見忌新主，謀人之義，可無慎哉；

translations.literal: Shizhi in sending off the late emperor had many lapses and was resented by the new sovereign—in the righteousness of plotting against others, can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi's role in the late emperor's death earned the new ruler's hatred; in such matters of conspiracy, caution is everything;

sentences.zh: 然晚遇誅夷，非其過也。

translations.literal: yet meeting execution late was not his fault.
translations.idiomatic: yet his late execution was hardly his fault alone.

sentences.zh: 毛喜逢時遇主，好謀而成，見廢昏朝，不致公輔，惜矣。

translations.literal: Mao Xi met the time and encountered his lord, loved strategy and achieved success, yet was cast aside in a benighted court and did not reach the highest ministers—a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xi met a worthy ruler and succeeded by counsel, yet was cast aside by a dissolute court and never reached the highest office—a pity.

sentences.zh: 沈、陸所以見重，固亦雅望之所致焉。

translations.literal: The reason Shen and Lu were valued was indeed also brought about by refined reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Lu were valued above all for their cultivated reputations.
